body:
Nothing crossed the arbitrage threshold today — the scanner returned zero opportunities across both platforms, which is the normal outcome on most scans and the case here.

Spot gold itself is quiet: it's trading near $4,383 as of Thursday, September 10, holding steady even as producer-price data pushed Treasury yields to nearly three-year highs. That level lines up neatly with what the Kalshi settle markets imply — the Gold price on September 30, 2026 contracts flip from favoring yes to favoring no right around the $4,330–$4,370 strikes, which is where you'd expect the crossover to sit if the market is pricing today's roughly $4,383 spot with over a year of drift still to come before that settlement date.

Two things worth flagging rather than trading on: first, several far-out-of-the-money Kalshi strikes (the $3,810.99 and $3,850.99 above contracts) show zero 24-hour volume — quotes there are stale, not tradable prices. Second, don't read cross-platform quote gaps as free money without checking mechanics: Kalshi's contracts are settle markets, resolving only on the price at one specific timestamp, while Polymarket runs a mix of touch markets (paying out if gold hits a level anytime during the whole window, e.g. the $4,300 in September contract at 77–83¢) and daily up/down bets. A touch contract and a settle contract on the same strike are pricing different questions, so a wide spread between them is usually a rule difference, not an exploitable edge. The Polymarket Up or Down on September 14 market, quoted 3¢/97¢, is also simply too thin and too far out to treat as informative.
headline: No arbitrage found; gold holds near $4,383 as Kalshi strikes bracket spot price
